message.content:
**Hydrogen – a quick‑reference cheat sheet**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.00794 u |
| | Atomic radius | ~53 pm |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Electron affinity | 72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Ionization energies (first three) | 13.598 eV, 27.211 eV, 40.964 eV |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.792847 µ_N |
| **Physical** | State at STP | Colorless, odorless, tasteless gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| | Density at STP | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume at 0 °C, 1 atm | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Heat capacity (Cp) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (298 K) |
| | Standard molar entropy | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Standard enthalpy of formation | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| **Chemical** | Diatomic molecule (H₂) | Most common form |
| | Flammability | Extremely flammable; explosive in air (1–4 % H₂ in air) |
| | Reactivity | Forms hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂), reacts with halogens, acids, and metals |
| | Hydrogen bonding | Strong intermolecular force in water, alcohols, etc. |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak base (forming hydronium) or acid (forming hydride) depending on partner |
| **Isotopic** | Protium (¹H) | 99.98 % natural abundance |
| | Deuterium (²H) | 0.02 % natural abundance; heavier, stable |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (half‑life ≈12.32 y); used in nuclear fusion & radiolabeling |
| | Isotopic masses | ¹H = 1.007825 u, ²H = 2.014102 u, ³H = 3.016049 u |
| | Isotopic effects | Deuterium substitution slows reaction rates (kinetic isotope effect) |
| **Nuclear** | Binding energy per nucleon | ~7.98 MeV (for ¹H) |
| | Nuclear reactions | Fusion (p + p → d + e⁺ + νₑ) powers the Sun; fusion of deuterium/tritium releases energy |
| | Applications | Fuel for fusion reactors, tracer studies, medical imaging (tritium), hydrogen fuel cells |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: only one proton (and usually one electron).
- **Highly reactive**: forms a wide range of compounds (hydrides, acids, organics).
- **Key in energy**: fuels hydrogen fuel cells; fuels nuclear fusion.
- **Isotopic diversity**: protium (stable), deuterium (stable), tritium (radioactive).
- **Unique chemistry**: forms strong hydrogen bonds, enabling water’s high boiling point and many biological processes.

Feel free to ask for deeper dives into any of these categories!
